r0.why: Bias as expected value minus true value [1]; averaging over all possible observations [12]; zero bias is unbiased [2]; objective property [3].

r1.why: Heading 'Why small bias is tolerated' presents a reason (implicitly the MSE point) that the cited sentences [5,6,21] never give as a cause for using biased estimators.

r2.why: Sample variance example [8]; naive estimator biased downward because sample mean from same data [19]; Bessel's correction unbiased [20].

r3.why: Bias distinct from consistency, consistent may be biased or not [4]; unbiased estimator need not exist [10]; binomial reciprocal example [11].

r4.why: Unbiasedness not guaranteed to carry over [15]; g(theta-hat) unless g linear [16]; mean-unbiasedness not preserved under non-linear transforms [8].

r5.why: ML bias can be substantial [35]; ticket box setup [36]; MLE is X, expectation (n+1)/2, n at least X [37]; 2X-1 unbiased [38].

r6.why: Bias w.r.t. median [7]; median-unbiased definition, under/over equally often [39]; exist where mean-unbiased and ML do not [42]; invariant under one-to-one [43].
